data.note: HumanChannel port, adapters, fake, relay through the ask engine, consent once per kind. Config/_core.py is held by UX-output-caps: glob added by update when free.

data.budget: 20 min, no network calls from code
data.claim: One port suffices: outbound adapters only post and report pending, the harness bridge couriers and reads through attest, the terminal collects; services/ask relays every collected answer through engine.answer, which already holds the digest and identity checks, so no adapter repeats them. No second notifier exists in ddflow today.
data.falsifier: An existing notify-send, osascript or smtplib implementation in ddflow, or a wire format of a target that cannot be expressed as one JSON POST with an optional bearer header.
data.mechanism: adapters is the bottom layer and cannot import the engine, so a channel returns data (Answer) and a service above records it. engine.answer refuses an actor whose source is not terminal, credential or named, and compares the presented digest with the row's. attest already records harness answers at level 2, so the bridge calls it rather than repeating it.
data.probe: grep -rnE 'notify-send|osascript|smtplib' ddflow; read services/ask/engine.py answer and _check_answerable, services/approvals/harness.py attest; opened the Slack, Teams and OpenClaw webhook docs
data.probe_output: grep exit 1 (no match). engine.answer: 'if actor.source not in ANSWER_SOURCES: raise AskRefused', _check_answerable compares digest != row['digest']. Slack: POST {"text": ...}, 200 'ok'. Teams: Office 365 connectors retired May 2026; Workflows webhook takes {"type":"message","attachments":[{contentType adaptive card}]}. OpenClaw: POST /hooks/agent {"message", "name"}, Authorization: Bearer hook token, query tokens rejected, 200 admitted.
data.question: Can one HumanChannel port (notify, ask, relay) cover terminal, harness bridge, desktop, email, Slack, Teams, webhook, n8n and OpenClaw, keeping the digest and person-only checks in the ask engine alone, with no existing notifier to fold in?

evidence.note: Research note recorded for ADP-notify-ask, CONFIRMED: grep for notify-send, osascript and smtplib in ddflow exits 1; engine.answer holds the digest and identity checks; Slack, Teams and OpenClaw wire formats read from their docs, each one JSON POST.

data.body: Split out of ADP-notify-ask so the port touched only its own files (r-adapters): a [notify] section needs config/_core.py, config/__init__.py, README.md and the goldens, all held by other lanes when it landed. (1) A [notify] section (channel, ask_channel, endpoints, token_env, send_timeout_s, ask_timeout_s, ask_attempts, email_host, email_port, email_from, email_to, email_user, email_password_env, email_tls) with the defaults of channels.Settings, a knob_added manifest each, README knob rows, goldens; channel and ask_channel are enums with the adapters as choices and the network ones outward. Settings.committed is derived from cfg.sources: every field whose source is 'file'. Acceptance: open_channel reads the knobs; an address set in the committed layer makes its adapter unavailable. (2) channels.grant_consent has no command: approval.grant is a person's terminal act, and r-approval-chat-channel wants a chat route. Add a gated site row and a verb so `approvals ask` and `attest` can grant consent for one kind, keeping consent once per kind (D-adapters-answers-3). r-consent-outward says consent expires; D-adapters-answers-3 says once per kind: ask the operator whether a kind's consent expires. Until this lands every network adapter reports unavailable.
data.title: [notify] knobs that fill services/ask/channels.Settings, and a chat route to grant a channel consent

evidence.note: ddflow_brief for the item and rule show: r-adapters (family files, fake, conformance, docs page, no shared file), r-approval-chat-channel (default ask channel is the harness bridge), r-consent-outward and D-adapters-answers-3 (consent once per kind, unavailable without it), r-secrets (no URL in a detail, committed address refused, tokens by variable name), r-small-files (each new module under 13 KB), r-everything-configurable (Settings now, knobs in ADP-notify-knobs).

Tests written first (import failed until the port existed). HumanChannel port with 9 registered adapters, FakeHumanChannel, relay through engine.answer, consent once per kind, docs page. tests/test_adapter_notify.py and tests/test_ask_channels.py pass (104 with the ratchets); selected run failures named against main are identical there: mcp.py size, stdio_safety, import_contracts, upstream url 8kb, status_surfaces_loops. Knobs deferred to ADP-notify-knobs because config/_core.py, README.md are held by other lanes.
